title: Player Strategies
objective: Design your own abstract base class for a player, implement three different strategies behind it, and add a --vs-computer mode to your CLI so the machine answers your moves. This is the second polymorphic hierarchy you write -- the first one was handed to you at Stage 5.

cpp: override and what it protects you from
git: reviewing your own diff before anyone else does

checks: `ttt-cli --vs-computer` runs, and after one move of yours the board has two marks.
Your move still lands exactly where you asked.
You have registered your own tests with ctest, and they pass.
Every contract test from Stage 5 still passes -- createGame() stays two-player.
Your blocking strategy takes an immediate win, and blocks an immediate loss (your tests prove this, not ours).
hints: Every strategy answers the same question -- 'given this board, where do you want to play?' -- in a different way. That sentence is a function signature. Write it down.
Your base class has no sensible default answer to that question, so its function has no body at all. Look up what `= 0` after a member function means, and what it makes the class.

Give the base class a `virtual` destructor. Without one, deleting a derived object through a base pointer only runs the base destructor -- and with AddressSanitizer on you can watch the leak happen.

For testing: seed your random generator with a fixed number (`std::mt19937 rng{12345}`) so the same game plays out the same way twice. Untestable randomness is a design choice, not a fact of life.

prompts.title: My override doesn't get called
prompts.body:
I have a base class and a derived class, and the derived version of my function is not being called.

Here is my code:
<PASTE IT>

Ask me: is the base function marked virtual, did I write `override` on the derived one, and am I holding the object by value or by pointer/reference? Walk me toward the answer by asking which of those I have checked, rather than telling me which one is wrong.

prompts.title: Review my class hierarchy
prompts.body:
I have designed an abstract Player base class with three strategy implementations for tic-tac-toe.

Here are my files:
<PASTE THEM>

Ask me questions about the design. Specifically: does my base class have a virtual destructor and can I say why it matters here, is chooseMove const and should it be, could a strategy return an illegal move and what happens if it does, and would adding a fourth strategy require changing any existing file? Do not rewrite it.

prompts.title: Quiz me for the interview
prompts.body:
Quiz me on virtual functions and polymorphism the way an interviewer would.

One question at a time, wait for my answer, and push back when I am vague. Cover at minimum: what a vtable is and when it gets used, why a base class needs a virtual destructor, what object slicing is and how to trigger it by accident, what `override` actually does for me, and the difference between overriding and overloading.

After each answer, tell me whether it would have satisfied an interviewer and what was missing.
